name: Visions of Glory
oracle_text:
Create a 1/1 white Human creature token for each creature you control.
Flashback {8}{W}{W}. This spell costs {X} less to cast this way, where X is the greatest mana value of a commander you own on the battlefield or in the command zone. (You may cast this card from your graveyard for its flashback cost. Then exile it.)
blocked_sentences: Flashback {8}{W}{W}. This spell costs {X} less to cast this way, where X is the greatest mana value of a commander you own on the battlefield or in the command zone.

needs.what: A cost-time value equal to the greatest mana value among the commanders one player owns, counting both the battlefield and the command zone -- e.g. a `commander_mana_value` value key (or a `{"greatest_mana_value": <filter>}` reduction shape) evaluated with `pick: "greatest"` over `state.players[pid].command` plus that player's commander permanents on the battlefield, read off the printed card (`state.card(oid).mana_value`) since a commander in the command zone has no board state.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: Three separate walls, and the value language clears none of them. (1) It is a maximum, not a sum: the reduction shapes `costs.reduction_amount` accepts are `{"amount": N}`, `{"count": filter}` and `{"total_power": filter}` -- the flat `amount` is a number written into the card, and the other two SUM over matches, so a player with two partner commanders would get their mana values added rather than the greater one, which is a different and larger number. (2) It cannot see the command zone: `costs._reduction_matches` iterates `state.battlefield` and nothing else, and it only reads `controller`/`types`/`subtypes`, so `is_commander` is not even one of the keys it honours -- yet the command zone is where a commander sits for most of a game, which is the case this card is written for. (3) Even inside `spell_effects`, where the richer language lives, it is not expressible as one number: `value_keys`' `max` takes a fixed list of value expressions written into the card (`values.py:300-301`), not a maximum over a selected pool; `mana_value_of` resolves a target, binding, snapshot or `self` (`values.py:314-336`) and cannot take a selector; and the `extreme` selector -- which does rank on `mana_value` (`selectors.py:195`, `selectors.py:226-234`) -- narrows an *object pool* and yields objects, not an integer, and `selectors.resolve_pool` builds that pool from exactly one `zone` (`selectors.py:175-188`), so it cannot span the battlefield and the command zone in a single selector even with `any_of` (which filters candidates, and never widens which zone they were drawn from). And all of this is moot for pricing anyway: a reduction is computed by `legality`/`game` before the spell is on the stack, where no `EffectContext` exists to evaluate a `value_keys` expression at all.

resolved_note: `conditional_cost_reduction` shipped, and it closed the *scoping* half of this card: a `mana_reduction` written inside the `flashback`/`graveyard_cost` CostModel is read by `costs.variant_reduction` from the flashback branch of `legality._cast_variant` and `game._cast` alone, so "costs {X} less to cast **this way**" no longer discounts the printed hand cast. The reduction may also carry a `condition`. What is still missing is only the *number*: `commander_mana_value`, below. Once it lands the answer is `{"op": "create_token", "token": "human_1_1_w", "amount": {"creatures_you_control": true}}` in `spell_effects` plus `{"flashback": {"mana": "{8}{W}{W}", "mana_reduction": {"greatest_mana_value": {"is_commander": true, "controller": "you", "zone": ["battlefield", "command"]}}}}`, with an expectation of `tokens` {"id": "human_1_1_w", "count": 2}, `battlefield_count` 34 and `zone` "graveyard".
rest_is_expressible: Sentence 1 loads today with no engine work: `{"op": "create_token", "token": "human_1_1_w", "amount": {"creatures_you_control": true}}` in `spell_effects` -- `create_token` is in `ops`, `creatures_you_control` is in `value_keys`, and `human_1_1_w` is already a registered token (`data/cards/zurgo.cards.json:147`: Creature, subtypes ["Human"], 1/1, colors ["W"]), so the `tokens` expectation key can assert it. The flashback *cast* is also already supported and is a card-level `flashback`/`graveyard_cost` CostModel with `graveyard_cast: "exile"` as its default -- `data/cards/zurgo.cards.json:236-273` is a white sorcery with `"flashback": {"mana": "{7}{W}{W}"}` and a `cast_from_graveyard` branch, i.e. this exact card one rider short. The rider's *slot* now exists too; only the {X} it takes does not. Writing the card as a bare `"flashback": {"mana": "{8}{W}{W}"}` would still be a card that is right about the price nobody pays and wrong about the price the card was designed around.
